title: The Bell That Rang Too Soon
passage:
At Midori Junior High, a short bell rang five minutes before the end of lunch. It was meant to remind students to finish eating and return trays before afternoon classes. For years, nobody questioned it. One month, however, the bell began ringing seven minutes early because the timer was accidentally changed during maintenance.

At first, most students simply followed the sound. They stood up, returned their trays, and left the lunch area earlier than usual. Teachers noticed that the hallway became crowded sooner, but they did not know why. A student named Reina finally looked at the wall clock and realized that the bell was not matching the schedule. She told a teacher, who checked the timer and found the error.

The simple mistake started a larger conversation. Reina's class wondered why everyone had obeyed the bell without checking the time. Some students said they trusted school signals because they were usually correct. Others admitted that they rarely looked at the clock during lunch. Their teacher said that routines are useful because they save mental effort, but routines can also make people stop noticing small changes.

For one week, the class paid attention to other automatic habits. They found that many students always used the same staircase even when another one was less crowded. Some threw paper into the nearest bin without checking whether it was for recycling. A few students opened their phones as soon as they sat down on the bus, even when they had not planned to use them. None of these habits were serious problems, but the students enjoyed noticing them.

After the timer was fixed, the bell once again rang at the correct time. Nothing about lunch changed in a dramatic way. Still, Reina began looking at the clock before standing up. She did not decide that routines were bad. Instead, she learned to treat them as helpful tools rather than unquestioned commands. A familiar signal can guide us efficiently, but every so often it is worth checking whether the signal still matches reality.
translation:
緑中学校では、昼休み終了の五分前に短いベルが鳴っていました。食事を終え、トレーを返し、午後の授業へ戻る準備をする合図です。長年、誰も特に疑問を持ちませんでした。ところがある月、点検の際にタイマー設定が変わり、ベルが七分も早く鳴るようになりました。

最初、生徒たちの多くは音に従い、いつもより早く立ってトレーを返しました。廊下が早い時間から混み始めましたが、先生たちは理由が分かりませんでした。レイナが壁時計を見て初めて、ベルと時刻が合っていないことに気づきました。先生が確認すると設定ミスが見つかりました。

この小さな失敗をきっかけに、『なぜ誰も時計を確認しなかったのか』という話になりました。学校の合図は普段正しいので信頼していたという生徒もいれば、昼休みに時計をほとんど見ないという生徒もいました。先生は、習慣は考える負担を減らしてくれる一方、変化に気づきにくくすることもあると説明しました。

クラスは一週間、他の無意識の習慣も観察しました。別の階段の方が空いていてもいつも同じ階段を使う、分別表示を確認せず一番近いごみ箱へ紙を入れる、使う予定がなくてもバスで座るとすぐスマートフォンを開く、といった行動が見つかりました。重大な問題ではありませんでしたが、気づくこと自体が面白かったのです。

タイマーが直ると、ベルは再び正しい時刻に鳴るようになりました。大きな変化はありませんでしたが、レイナは立つ前に時計を見るようになりました。習慣そのものが悪いのではありません。便利な道具として使い、ときどき現実と合っているか確かめることが大切だと学んだのです。
